amanda_lewis: quick sync — we need to finalize the PRD for the serving scheduler + prioritization work. customers are asking for predictable p99 and cheaper fallbacks; PM wants launch criteria by EOW. thoughts?

raj_patel: can we scope this so it's not a full kernel refactor? propose: 1) routing policy layer (rules) 2) lightweight attention path flags (hot swap) 3) KV eviction + prefix cache heuristics. keep the heavy kernel rewrites as follow-up.

julien_martin: +1 on incremental. also add acceptance criteria for compatibility: quantized variants must pass the same correctness evals or have explicit degradations documented.

sarah.chen: customers: FinProd and HealthData asked for 99th latency <= 250ms for 512 tokens baseline and max cost delta +8%. we should make these explicit. also need a rollback plan if fallback increases hallucination.

amanda_lewis: agreed. draft acceptance criteria (first pass):
- perf: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms (512 tokens, batch size 1)
- cost: average tokens/sec cost <= baseline * 1.08 for fallback policies
- correctness: output pass rate on smoke promptset >= 98% (same evals run in CI)
- safety: if model variant causes quality regression > 2% on critical eval, auto-fallback to previous variant

raj_patel: add operational criteria:
- telemetry: per-request kernel id, routing reason, seq_len, cache_hit boolean
- SLOs: 5min warmup SLA for autoscaled pools, canary rollout for new routing rules
- playbook: steps for manual rollback + automated circuit-breaker on error rate > 3%

julien_martin: edge cases to call out in PRD:
- mixed-precision mismatch between kernel and model (e.g., int8 kernel with fp16 model weights) -> block, require conversion or explicit model variant
- KV cache size mismatch causing OOM if route changes mid-session -> pin session to cache domain until end of conversation
- very long prefix (>8192 tokens) -> route to long-attn path, degrade to chunked decoding if memory under pressure

sarah.chen: QA/acceptance tests we need:
- regression suite: 2k prompts with golden outputs run against candidate routing rules + fallback combos
- perf harness: synthetic spike test (QPS 10x for 30s) + real traffic replay for 1 hour
- A/B quality test for hallucination delta using weighted human eval (sampled)

amanda_lewis: config example to include in PRD (for operator + console):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  priorities:
    - name: low_latency
      weight: 100
    - name: cost_saving
      weight: 30
  fallbacks:
    - condition: capacity_constrained
      target: model_variant:gptx-quant-8
    - condition: high_seq_len
      target: kernel:long-attn-v2
  cache:
    prefix_ttl: 600
    eviction: lru
```

raj_patel: love the config. add a note that prefix_ttl should be tunable per-tenant and that TTL=0 disables prefix caching. also we need to decide if session pinning is default or opt-in. pinning reduces throughput but avoids cache chaos.

julien_martin: recommendation: default opt-out pinning; set pinning=true for enterprise tier or when customer enables strict deterministic responses. document trade-offs in PRD.

sarah.chen: launch criteria checklist (proposal):
- PRD approved by eng/product/security
- Canary in 2 regions for 48h with no critical regressions
- Observability: dashboard + alerting for kernel errors, cache drift, quality regression metric live
- Docs: runtime config + migration guide + fallback behavior clearly documented
- Billing: cost model validated, Redwood Optimize recommendations updated

amanda_lewis: rollout plan: canary -> staged ramp -> enterprise opt-in -> global launch. we should set automated rollback triggers: error_rate > 2% OR quality_regression > 2.5% OR p99 > target for 30m. ops-bot: please create canary job after PRD approval.

ops-bot: scheduled job created: canary-deploy/serving-sched-priority at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z, notify: #eng-runtime, #eng-oncall

raj_patel: open questions for PM/legal/security:
- do we allow cross-tenant cache sharing for identical prefixes? privacy/security implications.
- acceptable data retention for prefix cache under compliance.

amanda_lewis: good callouts. mark both as blockers for GA. i'll add them to the PRD under "open decisions" and assign owners.

julien_martin: last nit: add a small section on metrics calculation (how we compute p99 under streaming responses and partial tokens) so there's no ambiguity for QA.

amanda_lewis: will do. timeline: PRD draft by tomorrow EOD, review on Thurs sync, sign-off Fri. thanks all. :rocket:
